### [x] SKILL-ROUTING-001 — Behavioral regression harness for skill/capability selection

- **Owner:** skill authority / generation-recipe assembly; a new provider-neutral
  evaluation harness, not a specification-to-source skill itself
- **Direction:** Skill and capability-contract selection is validated structurally today
  (schema shape, DAG acyclicity, exact pinned identities) but never behaviorally against
  real prompts/requests — nothing checks that the *right* skill actually gets selected
  for a given generation intent, or notices when one only appears to because its
  description's vocabulary happens to overlap a prompt rather than because the match is
  meaningful. Surfaced by surveying `example-web-tooling` (an internal, independently evolved,
  mature MCP server exposing ~35 `SKILL.md`-shaped web/frontend skills): its
  `scripts/diagnosis.ts`/`scripts/corpus.ts` run synthetic prompts against the real skill
  corpus and classify each outcome as correct pick, misroute (wrong skill won),
  over-greedy (a skill fired when it should not have), or fragile pass (the right skill
  matched, but the description's overlap with the prompt was thin enough that the match
  likely came from the model's training priors rather than the doc actually being read).
  This is a real, evidenced gap-class, not a hypothetical: this framework's own
  `COVERAGE-GAP-001`/#64 already establishes that a green build/test signal is not proof
  of completeness for *generation*; the same failure mode exists, unaddressed, for
  *skill/capability selection* upstream of generation.
- **Conclusion:** Add a provider-neutral evaluation harness that runs a corpus of
  synthetic generation prompts/requests against a project's actual skill and capability
  catalog and classifies each outcome the way `example-web-tooling`'s harness does (correct /
  misroute / over-greedy / fragile-pass), rather than only checking selection
  structurally. Scope it as a `litai`-level diagnostic (e.g. `litai skills evaluate` or
  similar), not a new specification-to-source skill, since its subject is the routing
  mechanism itself, not any one Component's generated source.
- **Depends on:** none; complements `SKILL-DEP-001`'s exact dependency-closure work
  (that resolves *what* gets pulled in once a skill is selected; this validates *that
  the right skill got selected* in the first place)
- **Implementation:**
  - [x] Added `src/literate_ai/skill_routing_evaluation.py`: loads every declared
        `specification-to-source` skill's real frontmatter `description`/`title` (via
        `parse_authoring_markdown`, the same raw-frontmatter parser
        `ResolvedSpecificationToSourceSkill.from_reference` uses internally but doesn't
        surface `description` from — it projects only the narrower typed manifest
        fields), tokenizes it, and scores it against a prompt.
  - [x] Fragile-pass detector: Jaccard overlap (`|intersection| / |union|`) between
        prompt and candidate tokens, not recall-on-prompt-only. Deliberately chosen
        after discovering recall-on-prompt structurally favors long, vocabulary-rich
        descriptions (this repository's own `generate-nvidia-cuda-application`
        description is far longer than its siblings' one-liners and won essentially
        every prompt under the naive formula purely by having more chances to share an
        incidental word) — Jaccard's union denominator makes a description's own
        irrelevant extra vocabulary work against it instead of for it. A small stopword
        list (function words, plus the literal "Use for Literate AI workflow tasks."
        boilerplate every skill description in this catalog shares) keeps unrelated
        prompts from over-firing on shared connective words.
  - [x] Corpus format: a JSON array of `{case_id, prompt, expected_skill_id}` (`null`
        expected means the prompt should route to nothing); `load_skill_routing_corpus`
        rejects malformed/duplicate/empty corpora and unknown `expected_skill_id`s
        before scoring anything.
  - [x] Wired as `litai skills evaluate CORPUS [--project PATH] [--fire-threshold N]
        [--fragile-threshold N]` (`src/literate_ai/cli/skills.py`), a new top-level
        command group parallel to `cache`/`catalog`, separate from `project validate`.
        Documented in `docs/user/configuration-and-cli.md`.
  - [x] Validated against this repository's own 17-skill catalog first:
        `tests/fixtures/skill_routing/literate_ai_catalog_corpus.json`, a 16-case seed
        corpus covering every language-portable-application skill, the two richer
        service/dashboard skills, two "should never fire" prompts, and one known-vague
        prompt.
- **Evidence:**
  - [x] Running the seed corpus against the real catalog reproducibly reports a
        `misroute` for a known-ambiguous pair
        (`portable-specification-planning`/`portable-application-implementation` — a
        real, informative finding: these two skills are semantically adjacent by
        design) and a `fragile_pass` for a genuinely thin match, not a silent
        correct-pick for either — `tests/smoke/test_skill_routing_evaluation.py::RealCatalogEvaluationTests::test_seed_corpus_mostly_routes_correctly_with_one_known_ambiguity`.
        A dedicated synthetic-fixture test
        (`test_known_ambiguous_pair_reproducibly_misroutes_or_fragile_passes`) makes the
        same property deterministic and independent of the real catalog's content
        drifting later.
  - [x] The harness never claims a selection is validated purely because it was
        structurally well-formed: `project validate`'s schema/DAG checks are entirely
        untouched by this work, and `evaluate_skill_routing` fails closed
        (`skill_routing.expected_skill_unknown`) rather than silently accepting a
        corpus that references a skill outside the real catalog.
  - [x] Full test suite (19 tests: scoring/classification, corpus loading, real-catalog
        evaluation, CLI wiring) passes; `litai skills evaluate` is reachable through the
        existing generic scoped-help mechanism (`litai help skills evaluate`) with no
        additional wiring.

### [x] GENERATION-008 — Detect an unusable selected coding CLI and fall back automatically

- **Release target:** 1.1.0

- **Priority:** P1
- **Owner:** `src/literate_ai/adapters/models/coding_cli.py` (`select_coding_cli`)
- **Direction:** `GENERATION-004`/#31 closed with a configurable priority order
  (`LITERATE_AI_CODING_CLI_PRIORITY`) but explicitly left open "a real usability/
  authentication probe... if a project needs per-host dynamic selection rather than a
  static configured order." That deferred case is no longer hypothetical: this session
  independently hit `codex` failing closed mid-release with "You hit your spend cap set
  by the owner of your workspace," requiring a manual `CODING_CLI=claude` override to
  make any progress on the `installed-project-e2e`/`samples` release gates. Surveying
  `~/Src/telemetry-dashboard` (an independent downstream project) found its own
  `verification/release-gate.sh` permanently hardcodes the identical override, with a
  comment citing the identical root cause ("`CODING_CLI` is pinned to claude per
  LITAI-001 (litai's own fixed codex-first default-CLI priority picks codex regardless
  of auth state)"). Two structurally unrelated projects independently converging on the
  same manual workaround for the same failure mode is a strong signal this belongs in
  the framework's default selection behavior, not in every project's own scripts.
- **Conclusion:** Extend `select_coding_cli` (or the point where a selected CLI's process
  is first invoked) to detect a fail-closed usability condition — authentication failure,
  spend-cap/quota rejection, or another CLI-reported hard denial distinguishable from
  ordinary generation flakiness — and fall through to the next entry in the configured
  priority order instead of surfacing the failure directly, at least for the specific,
  detectable "this CLI is currently unusable regardless of retry" class of error. Do not
  attempt a general authentication/capability probe run speculatively before every
  invocation (GENERATION-004 already considered and deferred that as the larger, less
  evidenced option); scope this to reacting to an already-observed hard denial.
- **Depends on:** `GENERATION-004`'s `LITERATE_AI_CODING_CLI_PRIORITY` mechanism
- **Implementation:**
  - [x] Enumerate only observed hard-denial signatures: Codex's workspace spend-cap
        wording and Claude's individual spend-limit wording (recorded during the
        RELEASE-006 live recovery above). Cursor Agent and OpenCode quota lists
        remain intentionally empty until a real denial is observed; each already
        retains its separate authentication-denial classification.
  - [x] Distinguish this class from ordinary transient generation flakiness: a new
        `coding_cli.quota_denied` typed error, checked only after the existing
        `coding_cli.authentication_required` classification (including its
        `login status` secondary probe) rules out an authentication cause, and only
        for a nonzero exit status — `GENERATION-006`'s `generated_metadata_invalid`
        retry path is untouched and stays exit-code-independent.
  - [x] On a detected hard denial (`authentication_required` or `quota_denied`), fall
        through to the next PATH-available CLI in the configured priority order (via new
        `_select_fallback_coding_cli`) for the remainder of the `generate()` call,
        logging `coding_cli_fallback` with the abandoned/adopted CLI names and reason.
        Bounded automatically: each attempted CLI name is tracked and excluded from
        further fallback, so the loop terminates once the priority order is exhausted
        and re-raises the last real denial (not a synthetic "exhausted" error).
  - [x] `CODING_CLI=<name>` (checked via the same truthy-env condition
        `select_coding_cli` itself uses) disables fallback entirely — a hard-denied pin
        raises immediately, never silently reroutes to a CLI the caller didn't ask for.
  - [x] Both `CodingCliSourceGenerator.generate()` and
        `CodingCliTaskRunner.run_json_task` apply the same bounded authentication/quota
        fallback. An explicit CLI pin or resolved generation model scope prohibits
        cross-provider fallback; select a healthy provider before locking that scope.
- **Evidence:**
  - [x] `tests/critical/test_coding_cli_generation.py::test_quota_denial_falls_back_to_the_next_available_cli`
        reproduces this session's exact scenario (codex denies with the real observed
        spend-cap phrase, `claude` is the next PATH-available CLI) and asserts the
        fallback CLI is invoked and the generation succeeds — no manual `CODING_CLI`
        override required.
  - [x] `tests.smoke.test_coding_cli_quota_fallback.CodingCliJsonTaskQuotaContractTests.test_json_task_quota_denial_falls_back_to_the_next_available_cli`
        covers the same fallback on `run_json_task` unless `CODING_CLI` is pinned.
  - [x] `test_explicit_coding_cli_pin_disables_fallback` and
        `test_quota_denial_reraises_original_error_when_fallback_is_exhausted` cover the
        two ways fallback must NOT silently mask a real denial: an explicit
        `CODING_CLI` pin, and a priority order with nothing left to fall back to.
  - [x] The full existing `test_coding_cli_generation.py` suite (108 tests, including
        every pre-existing authentication-classification and metadata-retry test) still
        passes unmodified — the new hard-denial branch never intercepts ordinary
        transient failures.
- **Current reconciliation:** Nine focused public generation/JSON-task regressions
  pass, including observed Claude denial, provider-specific classification, bounded
  exhaustion, explicit CLI pinning and resolved model-scope refusal. The JSON-task
  cases launch actual fixture executables; this closes the implemented fallback
  behavior without claiming that unknown provider quota signatures are recognized.

### [x] GENERATION-010 — Keep an explicit never-empty per-agent model stack

- **Priority:** P0
- **Release target:** 0.7.0
- **Re-scoped:** 0.9.0 (2026-09-01) for any remaining work; the historical target above records where the item originated / partially shipped.
- **Owner:** coding-session model cursor / specification language / spec-to-code
  converter
- **ADR:** [0018](../decisions/0018-never-empty-per-agent-model-stack.md)
  (Accepted 2026-08-26)
- **Direction:** Coding sessions keep an explicit model stack. Frame 0 is the
  session model. Nested Component, Flavor, skill, and in-spec sectional changes
  push when the model changes and pop when leaving. Push, pop, and depth are
  part of the specification language. Each thread and each agent has its own
  stack. Popping the only remaining frame is a warning that logs the precise
  caller. Never go to stack depth 0.
- **Conclusion:** The lexical `ModelScopeBinding` stays the lock/cache identity.
  The runtime cursor is a `contextvars` stack that is never empty after
  `begin_session`. A last-frame pop is refused with `ModelStackPopRefusedWarning`
  and a `model.stack.pop_refused` event naming file, line, function, and any
  specification location. Do not use a process-global list. Do not wait on
  [ADR 0011](../decisions/0011-component-domain-structure-literate-markdown-v2.md)
  for sectional directives.
- **Depends on:** [GENERATION-011](#generation-011-pin-live-qualification-to-an-explicit-user-configured-cli-and-model)

### [x] ROADMAP-OWNERSHIP-001 — Keep parent and downstream work with their owners

- **Priority:** P0
- **Owner:** roadmap governance and `record-user-directed-work`
- **Direction:** A child project may expose a defect or reusable improvement owned
  strictly by a parent Component or repository. Send that change to the parent when the
  agent has Git access; otherwise retain it in the child's own repository. Conversely,
  Literate AI must not absorb a downstream product's mission vocabulary, milestones,
  repository paths, or release gates merely because that product exposed a framework
  defect.
- **Conclusion:** Classify ownership before editing. Put provider-neutral parent
  contracts, fixtures, and reusable guidance in the parent. With authenticated write
  access, contribute them through a reviewable parent branch/commit or pull request,
  never an unreviewed direct-default-branch mutation. Without access, keep the local
  override or proposed patch and its work item in the child. Product recovery and
  qualification always remain in the downstream queue. Reciprocal work-item, commit, or
  pull-request references preserve traceability without making either repository's
  release gate depend directly on the other.
- **Depends on:** repository lineage, project-local durable work queues, and the
  detailed-roadmap lifecycle
- **Implementation:**
  - [x] Remove downstream product names and product-owned recovery checks from generic
        cache, bounded-context, repository-update, and candidate-repair work items.
  - [x] Teach the framework and initialized-project work-recording skills to classify
        parent-owned changes, contribute them upstream when authorized, and retain them
        locally when upstream Git access is unavailable.
  - [x] Record the affected product qualification in its own repository without moving
        any product Component or mission policy into Literate AI.
- **Evidence:**
  - [x] A repository-wide authority search finds no downstream product identifier in
        Literate AI source, skills, tests, samples, or the active roadmap.
  - [x] SkillEvaluator passes both changed inherited skill surfaces, and 52 focused

        inherited, while both repositories retain independently executable gates.

### [x] UPDATE-APPLY-001 — `litai update --apply` must not abort the whole transaction on one catalog-import collision

- **Priority:** P1
- **GitHub issue:** [#133](https://github.com/NVIDIA-dev/literate-ai/issues/133)
- **Owner:** `src/literate_ai/adapters/repository_updates.py` (`_updated_imports`)
- **Direction:** `litai update .` (plan-only) correctly classifies files per-file
  (`unchanged`/`local-only`/`preserved-dynamic`/`upstream-only`/`upstream-added`/
  `conflict`), but `--apply` aborted the *entire* operation the moment
  `_updated_imports` found even one (kind, name) catalog-import identity collision
  between a locally tracked import and the freshly recomputed inherited plan —
  writing none of the plan's already-known-safe `upstream-only` files, not even ones
  structurally unrelated to the colliding item. Reproduced against
  `example-org/telemetry-dashboard`: 3 genuinely safe `upstream-only` skill files were
  blocked by an unrelated `flavor:javascript` conflict the project had deliberately
  and knowingly diverged from upstream.
- **Conclusion:** A catalog-import identity collision means the project's existing
  local provenance record for that one key should stay authoritative (not be
  overwritten by the inherited recomputation) — it never meant every other file's
  already-correct per-file classification should be discarded. `_updated_imports` now
  drops only the colliding inherited entries (keeping the existing local record
  intact) instead of raising; every file's write eligibility remains governed
  independently by `plan()`'s existing per-file classification exactly as before,
  which already keeps a diverged item's own files out of the safe `upstream-only` set
  regardless of this catalog-level fix. Confirmed this does not create a
  content/provenance mismatch: a file only ever writes when its own identity-based
  classification says `upstream-only`, independent of what the colliding entry's
  metadata claims.
- **Implementation:**
  - [x] Changed `_updated_imports`'s collision handling from
        `raise RepositoryUpdateError("repository_update.provenance_conflict", ...)` to
        silently excluding colliding `(kind, name)` entries from the inherited set,
        keeping the project's existing local (`kept`) entry unchanged for that key.
  - [x] `repository_update.provenance_conflict` is no longer raised by ordinary
        collisions; the error class/code remain defined for other genuine failure
        paths in the same module.
- **Evidence:**
  - [x] `tests/smoke/test_repository_updates.py::test_different_repository_import_collision_keeps_the_local_entry`
        (renamed from `..._remains_fail_closed`, which asserted the now-superseded
        hard-abort behavior) — a foreign-sourced local import collides with an
        inherited recomputation; `apply()` no longer raises, the local provenance
        record is preserved unchanged, and (since that file's content was already
        identical to baseline) nothing gets rewritten.
  - [x] `test_catalog_import_collision_does_not_block_unrelated_safe_files` — the
        direct reproduction of #133's report: one colliding catalog item (`python`,
        foreign-sourced) alongside a second, genuinely upstream-changed item
        (`macos`); the `macos` file classifies and applies as `upstream-only` while
        the `python` collision is preserved untouched, in the same `apply()` call.
  - [x] Full `tests/smoke/test_repository_updates.py` suite (9 tests, including the two
        above) passes.

  most ten paths and `--json` prints SHA identities. Operators and LLMs cannot
  judge a conflict without fetching the three blobs themselves.

  and do not auto-merge. Distinct from `UPDATE-MERGE-001` / ADR 0007.

        already available to the classifier.

        not set.

- **Previous release target:** 0.4.1 — deferred out of 0.3.0 scope; not on the 0.3.0
  release-blocking path.
- **Owner:** package contracts and adapters, `litai package`, release policy,
  initialized-project authority, and the built-in package Flavor catalog
- **Direction:** Every releasable Component must package its authoritative
  specification together with its accepted final build/executable products when the
  Component selects a package type. Support pip wheels on Linux, macOS, and Windows as
  the default package Flavor; Conan on all three operating systems as the portable
  wildcard choice; apt on Linux; Homebrew on macOS; and WinGet or Chocolatey on
  Windows. Expose these as first-class `package.<name>` Flavors and make packaging an
  explicit release-engineering phase.
- **Conclusion:** Preserve the existing exact `PackagePlan`/`PackageResult` boundary,
  but add the missing user-facing lifecycle and provider policy above it. Package
  construction must never imply repository publication: `litai package plan`,
  `build`, and `verify` operate on exact accepted artifacts, while `litai release`
  consumes verified package evidence and retains a separately authorized publish
  phase. A Component with no package tag is not packaged implicitly during an ordinary
  build, but release preparation must fail if a tagged Component lacks its current
  verified package. The package Flavor owns native format/tool requirements and OS
  compatibility; specifications own only the product's decision to select a package.
  Wildcard package selection resolves Conan for cross-language Components, while an
  otherwise unpinned Python-capable Component defaults to a pip wheel. Packaging is a
  multi-value Flavor slot: repeated compatible package selections create independent
  plans and results over the same accepted artifact closure so one repository can serve
  multiple user communities. Native formats are not mutually exclusive merely because
  they share the packaging axis; OS constraints, not artificial pairwise conflicts,
  reject impossible combinations.
- **Depends on:** the existing Standard artifact graph, post-build CycloneDX evidence,
  package-plan contracts, Flavor compatibility resolution, and RELEASE-001
- **Next action:** Three-OS live native fixtures and release-prepare package
  evidence remain. `--worker` routing is landed without artifact export.

### [ ] INDEX-001 — Stop CodeGraph ignore rules from hiding real generated source

- **Release target:** 1.1.0
- **Previous release target:** 0.9.0 (re-scoped 2026-09-01: had no explicit target)
- **Priority:** P0 — currently blocks the `samples` release gate deterministically.
- **Owner:** `src/literate_ai/adapters/intelligence/codegraph.py`, JavaScript
  specification-to-source skills
- **Direction:** The `samples` gate fails reproducibly with
  `source-index.codegraph-failed`. Root cause (confirmed by instrumenting
  `_require_source_binding`): `_status_source_paths`'s `ignored_directories` set skips
  any directory literally named `build` (alongside `dist`, `out`, `target`, …) when
  walking a non-Git generated tree. The JavaScript sample legitimately generates real
  application sources at `source/build/bundle.js` and `source/build/clean.js`, so the
  indexed snapshot omits exactly those two files while the caller's exact file manifest
  includes them. The two lists then disagree and indexing fails closed:

  ```
  expected: (…, 'source/build/bundle.js', 'source/build/clean.js', 'source/lib.js', …)
  indexed:  (…,                                                   'source/lib.js', …)
  ```

  Those ignore names are a sensible default for a *human* repository but wrong for a
  generated tree whose exact file manifest is already known and authoritative.
- **Conclusion:** Decided: `_status_source_paths`'s non-Git fallback walk only ever runs
  for a generated tree in this codebase (a human repository always has `.git`, so it
  takes the `_git_visible_paths` path instead), so the ignore list never needs to guess
  between "human repository" and "generated tree" — it is always the latter. Split the
  ignore set instead of threading a manifest parameter through every caller (rejected
  candidate 1/2: `_status_source_paths` is shared by `ensure_index`, `query`, and
  `relationship_evidence`, and those must all recompute the identical deterministic
  snapshot for a given tree regardless of caller context — a per-call manifest parameter
  would make `ensure_index`'s indexed set diverge from a later `query`'s re-snapshot of
  the same tree and break the existing `operational_binding` stability invariant).
  Names that are exclusively dependency/tool caches (`node_modules`, `.venv`, `Pods`,
  `.cache`, …) remain unconditionally ignored — a generation skill never legitimately
  emits real source there. Ambiguous build-artifact-style names (`build`, `dist`, `out`,
  `target`, `obj`, `coverage`, `.build`) are no longer ignored, since a generation skill
  can legitimately choose them for real generated output, and the existing
  `maximum_status_snapshot_files`/`maximum_status_snapshot_bytes` bounds already fail
  closed if a generated tree somehow contains something huge. Rejected candidate 3
  (forbid generated trees from using those names) for the reason already stated in
  Direction: it pushes an indexing-implementation detail into skill authority.
- **Evidence:**
  - [x] A focused unit test
    (`test_project_source_index.py::ProjectSourceIntelligenceTests::test_non_git_tree_inventories_generated_source_under_build`)
    proves a generated tree containing `source/build/bundle.js` is inventoried. The
    ignore set is caches-only (`node_modules`, `.venv`, …); `build`/`dist` are visible.
  - [ ] The `samples` gate passes without the JavaScript sample being special-cased —
    not yet run from this revision; needs a `make samples` (or equivalent CI) pass to
    close this item.

### [x] RELEASE-OBS-001 — Report what the release gate said when it fails

- **Priority:** P0
- **Owner:** `src/literate_ai/project_releases.py`
- **Direction:** `litai release check` ran the declared gate with
  `capture_output=True` and, on failure, raised
  `release gate failed with exit status 2` while discarding the gate's stdout and
  stderr entirely. The gate is the longest step in a release, so a failure yielded one
  uninformative integer after a multi-hour run and the operator had to re-run
  `make release-check` by hand to learn which check failed. During 0.3.0 this wasted a
  complete gate run.
- **Conclusion:** Carry a bounded, whitespace-collapsed tail of the gate's own output
  into the raised error, preferring stderr and falling back to stdout, and say so
  explicitly when the gate produced no output at all. Bounded rather than a full
  transcript, because the gate emits megabytes of conformance JSON.
- **Implementation:**
  - [x] `_release_gate_failure_detail` summarizes a failed gate; `check_release`
    includes it in `release.gate_failed`.
- **Evidence:**
  - [x] `tests/e2e/test_project_releases.py::ReleaseGateFailureDetailTests` proves
    stderr preference, stdout fallback, the silent-gate message, and that the detail is
    bounded while keeping the tail.

### [x] FLAVOR-006 — Add a Flavor to an existing project without re-initializing

- **Milestone:** 0.4.1
- **Owner:** `litai` CLI (a new Flavor-composition verb), lock planning, project authority
- **Direction:** User feedback: "There is no way to add a Flavor to an existing project."
  A project started on macOS that later needs Linux support has no incremental path --
  the only route is `litai init` into a fresh tree plus a manual merge, which is wrong
  for what is conceptually a mixin.
- **Conclusion:** Treat a Flavor as a mixin that can be composed into an existing
  project. Adding one must fully re-derive the dependency graph, capability
  requirements, toolchain constraints, and every affected Component lock -- the
  correctness properties of a fresh init -- while leaving authored Components,
  specifications, and history in place. It is a re-resolution, not a re-scaffold.
- **Open questions to settle before implementing:**
  - Does this become `litai flavor add <selector>`, an extension of `litai update`, or a
    `--flavor` argument on an existing verb? Naming should make the re-resolution
    explicit rather than implying a mere edit.
  - Removal and conflict: `-flavor` selectors already exist for init; adding
    `flavor://literate-ai/lang-go` to a project pinned to a conflicting Flavor must fail
    closed with the same cross-axis rules `_require_flavor_relations` enforces today.
  - Which Component locks must be invalidated, and can any legitimately survive.
  - What the operation writes when a newly required toolchain is absent on the host.
- **Evidence:**
  - [x] A macOS-initialized project gains `os-linux` incrementally; authored Component
    Markdown is unchanged and `component.lock.json` beside it is deleted so the next
    lock re-derives. Full `litai project validate` after mixin remains a follow-up.
  - [x] Adding a conflicting Flavor (`python` + `go`) fails closed and mutates nothing.
  - [x] Adding a Flavor twice is a no-op rather than a duplicate contribution.

### [ ] PLUGIN-001 — Ship standardized coding-CLI plugins with every release

- **Priority:** P1 (1.1 release engineering)
- **Release target:** 1.1.0
- **Owner:** release packaging, the canonical skill catalog, coding-CLI plugin adapters,
      and `litai package` / `litai release`
- **Direction:** Create standardized coding-CLI plugins as part of the release-engineering
      cycle. Most operators should not need to learn the `litai` CLI before an agent can
      follow the framework, and a release must not leave its agent integration artifacts
      as an unrelated manual packaging exercise.
- **Conclusion:** Define one provider-neutral plugin-bundle contract from the checked-in
      root and agent skills, then project that exact content through thin adapters for each
      supported coding CLI with a declared plugin format. Codex and Claude are the initial
      concrete adapters; Cursor and OpenCode must have an explicit supported or unsupported
      result rather than an invented format. Build, verify, and publish the applicable
      plugin artifacts from the same prepared revision as the wheel. Keep `litai` usable
      directly; plugins are distribution adapters, not a second implementation.
- **Depends on:** the existing generated skills bundle and `litai-mcp`; the release artifact
      policy must admit the standardized plugin bundle before publication becomes a gate
- **Next action:** Complete and qualify the local packaging prototype against
      [ADR 0039](../decisions/0039-1.1-capability-boundaries.md)'s accepted support matrix. Manifest validation
      and reproducibility tests pass; full routed-skill closure and fresh provider-session
      generation remain unqualified. No marketplace or ambient configuration was changed.
- **Constraints:**
  - Plugin bundles reuse the canonical checked-in skills and bind their distribution
    version and content identities; no hand-maintained second skill copy is allowed.
  - Installation never silently changes user configuration, credentials, permissions, or
    MCP registrations. Provider-specific setup remains explicit and reviewable.
  - Provider adapters may change packaging shape, never framework behavior or acceptance
    semantics.
- **Implementation:**
  - [x] Generate the existing skills bundle from checked-in skill files and prove there is
        no second maintained copy (`make plugin-bundle`, `tests.smoke.test_plugin_bundle`).
  - [ ] Define and validate one versioned, provider-neutral plugin-bundle manifest.
  - [ ] Project reproducible Codex and Claude plugin artifacts and record explicit Cursor
        and OpenCode support decisions.
  - [ ] Integrate applicable plugin artifacts into package, release prepare/check, and
        published-release verification for the exact prepared revision.
  - [ ] Document explicit installation, upgrade, and removal without mutating ambient

### [ ] PACKAGE-002 — Publish a Homebrew formula for literate-ai itself

- **Release target:** 1.1.0
- **Previous release target:** 0.9.0 (re-scoped 2026-09-01: had no explicit target)
- **Milestone:** 0.4.1
- **Owner:** release publication, packaging
- **Direction:** User feedback: `brew install literate-ai` should work on macOS instead
  of requiring `make install` from a checkout.
- **Distinction worth keeping straight:** `flavors/brew` already exists, but it is the
  packaging Flavor that lets *generated applications* produce Homebrew packages. It does
  not package literate-ai itself. This item is a Homebrew formula for the distribution.
- **Conclusion:** `make install` already does the substantive work correctly -- an
  isolated virtualenv beneath `${PREFIX}/share/literate-ai/venv` and a stable `litai`
  launcher in `${PREFIX}/bin`. A formula expresses that through Homebrew's
  `Language::Python::Virtualenv`. The formula is the easy part; the prerequisites are
  the work.
- **Depends on:**
  - A published release artifact with a stable tarball URL and sha256, which is the
    `litai release publish` step. This item is therefore downstream of 0.3.0 shipping.
  - A decision on CodeGraph, which literate-ai requires at 1.1.1+ and which installs via
    npm today. The formula must either declare a `node` dependency and provision it, or
    keep the current detect-and-bootstrap behavior. `brew install` should leave a
    working tool.
- **Open question:** a dedicated public tap (immediate) versus
  homebrew-core (notability requirements, slower).
- **Evidence:**
  - [ ] `brew install` on a clean macOS host yields a working `litai` that passes
    `litai project validate` on a freshly initialized project.

  host configuration. This is not a hard readiness requirement: missing privilege, a

  is present. Do not install NTP packages solely for this attempt, and do not fail
  `passed` when sync fails.

  specification roots

        only when the offset is large; Windows uses `w32tm` without a persistent-config

  - [x] Keep bootstrap `passed` coupled only to missing sample-worker capabilities.

### [~] GRAPH-001 — Solve, explain, and export effective repository inheritance DAGs

- **Release target:** 1.1.0

- **Priority:** P0
- **Owner:** framework repository-lineage, inherited-catalog, validation, and graph
  introspection contracts
- **Direction:** Give engineers one comprehensive graph solver and graph-export surface
  for reasoning about what a Literate AI project owns, what it inherits through its
  complete repository-parent chain, and what each entity deliberately withholds through
  `inheritable: false`. Use the same graph to reject cycles and to identify reusable
  Components, Flavors, and skills that are candidates to migrate upward when a
  multi-repository hierarchy becomes unnecessarily flat or duplicated.
- **Conclusion:** Build one immutable, provenance-aware effective-authority DAG rather
  than separate inheritance, validation, visualization, and rebalance implementations.
  Nodes must identify repositories and typed entities; edges must distinguish repository
  parentage, entity inheritance/ownership, Component dependencies, Flavor/skill
  selections, and explicit shadowing or withholding. Deterministic solving must happen
  before update, reparent, validate, build, test, or run can consume inherited authority.
  Exporters are pure views over the solved graph. Rebalance is advisory: it may report
  common ancestors, duplication, fan-in/fan-out, context-cost estimates, and proposed
  upward moves, but it must never relocate authority or push to another repository
  without an explicit reviewed operation.
- **Scope boundary:** Do not turn `litai` into a repository manager, task scheduler, or
  automatic refactoring bot. Do not infer semantic equivalence merely from matching
  names. Recommendations require exact identities or explicitly proven compatibility,
  preserve authored ownership and `inheritable` decisions, and report conflicts rather
  than selecting a winner silently.
- **Depends on:** repository-lineage and reparent contracts, inherited initialization and
  update provenance, Component locking, effective Flavor/skill selection, and current
  CodeGraph/project-validation prerequisites
- **Next action:** Extend rebalancing beyond exact duplicates with explicit compatibility
  and context-cost evidence; lifecycle preparation and initialization now use portable,
  graph-bound lock/audit authority.
- **Implementation:**
  - [x] Define a versioned canonical graph contract with stable node/edge identifiers,
        typed edge kinds, origin repository/revision, inheritance disposition, effective
        owner, shadowing/withholding evidence, and content identity.
  - [x] Resolve the complete multi-parent repository DAG deterministically, detect cycles
        with a minimal reproducible cycle path, reject ambiguous authority/collisions,
        and compute effective inherited versus project-local entity sets.
  - [~] Replace parallel lineage/catalog walks in init, update, reparent, validate, lock,

### [x] CONVERSION-DIAGNOSTICS-001 — Preserve bounded root-cause evidence from long baselines

- **Priority:** P0 (host-heavy conversion failures currently lose their actionable
      error and record an identity for only an initial output prefix)
- **Release target:** 0.9.0
- **GitHub issue:** [#298](https://github.com/NVIDIA-dev/literate-ai/issues/298)
- **Owner:** retained-harness process output and conversion failure boundary
- **Observed behavior:** A synthetic command whose stdout exceeds 1 MiB records neither
      its first `ROOT-ERROR` nor its final `ACTUAL-TAIL`; the purported tail is the end
      of the first 1 MiB. Its `stdout_identity` also hashes that prefix rather than the
      complete 1,100,024-byte stream. Any nonempty generic stderr then hides stdout
      entirely in the public failure message. The first exact native rerun after the
      stream repair proves a second boundary: the inner excerpt contains the GLIBC
      failure, but the public JSON message is exactly 512 characters and ends at the
      stdout head.
- **Conclusion:** Temporary files already provide file-backed custody, but the reader
      seeks to byte zero and reads only `limit + 1` bytes before excerpting, hashing,
      test-summary observation, and verbose tracing. Preserve the complete stream's
      digest while retaining bounded head/error/tail windows; combine labeled stdout
      and stderr diagnostics instead of choosing one stream. Make the effective finite
      capture policy explicit and evidence-bound rather than introducing an unrecorded
      process-global override. Preserve the ordinary CLI's 512-character safety bound,
      but let the two conversion gate errors carry their already validated finite
      diagnostic budget through the final envelope.
- **Competing hypotheses:** A twelve-line/1,500-character tail alone is insufficient
      but does not explain the missing physical tail or incorrect digest. Log overwrite,
      stale receipts, and redaction are contradicted by a fresh direct invocation of
      `_run_harness_command`; the bytes remain present in its temporary file until the
      post-process reader discards them.
- **Falsification:** The theory is wrong if a full-stream digest plus bounded
      head/error/tail scan still omits synthetic first and final markers, or if the
      recorded identity does not match an independently computed SHA-256 of the entire
      stream.
- **Implementation:**
  - [x] Factor a constant-memory file-backed output observer that computes full-stream
        identity and preserves bounded head, first error contexts, and tail.
  - [x] Record the effective output/diagnostic limits in baseline and parity evidence;
        validate any operator override at the CLI boundary and apply one identical
        policy to direct and wrapper executions.
  - [x] Keep receipts and user-facing diagnostics bounded and secret-redacted; never
        retain complete command output in committed evidence.
  - [x] Propagate only conversion build/CI gate budgets through the CLI dispatcher;
        retain the 512-character default for every other error and a hard 66,048
        character ceiling for all callers.
- **Validation:**
  - [x] Prove full digest, first/root error, actual tail, mixed stdout/stderr reporting,
        oversized-success policy, test-summary discovery, and invalid-bound rejection
        with contract tests.
  - [x] The focused 190-test diagnostics, conversion-flow, CLI, and evidence slice has
        189 behavioral passes; its sole pre-review failure is the expected stale
        documentation-authority marker. After recording the reviewed authority, the
        canonical self-description regression passes and the final-code complete
        Python gate passes 3,370 tests with 30 expected skips.
  - [x] The native Animation Authoring rerun retains the first actionable CentOS 7
        `GLIBCXX` incompatibility plus bounded head and tail evidence while preserving
        the 7,200-second timeout, byte-clean rollback, and source-parity behavior.

    existing portable `fcntl.flock`/`msvcrt.locking` primitive from

### [ ] MAC-CONTRACT-002 — Make the framework's own harness a projectable lifecycle selection

- **Release target:** 1.1.0

- **Owner:** MAC repository contract projection; framework self-description
- **Direction:** `litai project mac-contract` can project a MAC contract for any Component this
      project builds, but not for the Literate AI Python harness itself. Every one of the 163
      resolved BOMs under `_build` describes a sample Component.
- **Conclusion (corrected 2026-09-08):** an earlier revision of this item claimed MAC onboarding
      was blocked on this. That was wrong, and the error is worth recording. MAC's
      `register_project` is explicit that "the contract is the onboarding task's *output*, not a
      precondition": `mac project register URL` mints an onboarding task carrying
      `origin.onboarding`, which is exempt from the repository-contract guard
      (`mac/services.py:6024`). The guard only rejects the half-state produced by setting a
      project's `repository_url` *without* registering a repository — which is what an incorrect
      manual `project create` + `project update --registration` sequence produces. Two distinct
      questions were conflated: (a) what a MAC runner needs to check out this repository and run
      its own gates — answerable from the declared `make bootstrap` / `make python-check`
      entrypoints, and the question MAC onboarding actually asks; and (b) what a Literate AI
      *project's* build closure requires, which is what
      `skills/agent/write-mac-project-contract/SKILL.md` governs and which does need a
      post-build BOM. Only (b) is this item. Applying (b)'s CycloneDX-only rule to (a) caused a
      fleet onboarding attempt to return an investigation with no contract file.
- **Depends on:** none
- **Implementation:**
  - [ ] Model the framework's own Python distribution as a selection whose lifecycle emits a
        post-build resolved CycloneDX BOM, so `litai project mac-contract` can describe the
        harness rather than a sample
  - [ ] Confirm the projection's `required_commands` names only what the harness needs; a darwin
        `playback-controller` BOM yields `dyld_info, git, litai, make, python3.14, xcrun`, which
        is that sample's native closure and would break any declared `linux` runner
- **Evidence:**
  - [ ] The projected `required_commands` contains no sample-specific native toolchain entries
  - [ ] Re-running the projection produces byte-identical `.mac/project.yaml` and
        `.mac/project.contract.json`

      qualified keys must also cover the actual run interval. Correctly signed
      assertions still fail for substituted subject/media/context, prior invocations,
      stale or future runs, excessive duration, non-passing terminal status and reduced
      matrix coverage. Authorized locator assertions require matching object/store
      scope and sufficient claimed retention. Check results bind exact authenticated
      bytes plus policy, revocation and independent expectation identities.
      All 113 trust, storage, signature, schema, architecture and wheel/custody tests
      pass in 6.511 seconds. The expanded installed probe passes from source with
      policy-checked storage/resolution and wrong-revision refusal; its exact installed
      qualification is pending. This does not implement OIDC/CI certificate validation,
      authenticated transitive closure, post-resolution revocation refresh, retained
      availability or receipt promotion; the remaining OPS-300 tasks stay open.
- **Implemented storage ports:** Explicit filesystem, checked-out monorepo and HTTPS
      stores now supply immutable objects through `EvidenceStore`. The configured
      `EvidenceResolver` snapshots routing and checks all reference/locator metadata
      and operation bounds before I/O, then rechecks returned byte size and digest.
      Missing mirrors may fall back; corrupt mirrors and conflicting locator metadata
      fail closed. Read-only filesystem access creates no directories or locks.
      HTTPS uses certificate/hostname validation, explicit credentials, exact media
      and length, no redirects or encodings, and conditional PUT followed by a verified
      GET. The real-TLS refusal regression exposed deferred response cleanup while an
      exception traceback remained live; explicit response closure fixes that leak.
      The 104 storage, signature, schema, architecture, CAS-bound and wheel/custody
      tests pass in 5.886 seconds. They include real TLS publication/readback,
      signed-statement resolution, corruption, missing/duplicate references, bounded
      reads, stalled-body timeout, and filesystem/monorepo behavior. The expanded
      installed probe passes from source and will qualify signed statement storage,
      resolution and missing-blob refusal from the next exact non-editable wheel.
      Direct-reference resolution is implemented; authenticated recursive closure,
      claimed-retention admission and receipt promotion remain open.
- **Implemented evidence contracts:** Four closed v2 derivation-run, platform-run,
      matrix and locator predicates are published in the current schema catalog and
      carried by standard in-toto statements inside bounded DSSE envelopes. Run context
      binds exact repository/revision/workflow/target and invocation/time values.
      Immutable named artifact collections and matrix coverage reject duplicates,
      missing declared cells and wrong envelope media. Locators name explicitly
      configured stores and immutable objects, never ambient URLs or paths.
      Local PyCA Ed25519 verification precedes one parse of the exact signed bytes;
      it retains those original bytes and authenticates distinct configured keys.
      Standard envelope/statement extensions are ignored; predicate extensions are
      rejected. Neither a signature nor the producer's own matrix requirements or
      retention deadline establishes admission policy. The combined evidence,
      isolation-schema, catalog, architecture and frozen-schema suite passes 73 tests
      in 5.572 seconds, including substitutions, invalid signatures, thresholds,
      malformed/oversized JSON, closed-field refusal, time order and matrix coverage.
- **Installed qualification:** At `9ed02d16`, the installed signature probe passed but
      worker wheelhouse export rejected CFFI 2.1.1's three valid empty ZIP directories.
      The validator now admits those entries while rejecting links, startup hooks,
      traversal, colliding paths and unrecorded regular files. Adjacent component-sorted
      path comparison also avoids quadratic prefix allocation; its 8 KiB deep-name
      regression caught 34,361,369 bytes before repair and passes an 8 MiB ceiling.
      The 54 focused worker/DSSE/wheel-custody tests pass in 1.433 seconds.
      Exact `bf6d3d90` subsequently passed the complete installed-wheel gate, including
      native dependency wheelhouse installation and signature round-trip/tamper checks:
      wheel `sha256:bd66aef9b7981d121c57e78ddcb4f4ebbf0cc6c21670ed839e02b0dd9a220f90`,
      evidence run `20260912T233546Z-96d3b6`, retained stdout 18,138 bytes with

### Repository lifecycle lock custody repair (#418 / #425)

The integration review reproduced execution continuing after a child replaced
`execution.lock`, followed by unconditional deletion of the replacement. The executor
now reuses descriptor-backed write reservations and checks ownership around commands,
with setup inside the reservation cleanup scope. Regressions cover replacement with
foreign and identical bytes, edits, and failed receipt setup. A 43-test run exposed
reservation error translation masking a missing-product failure; acquisition now
translates only its own failures and preserves execution errors. The combined reservation, lifecycle, refresh and version-authority run passes
90 tests in 397.640 seconds on macOS. Renaming an open CRT file is explicitly
unsupported in the Windows replacement fixtures; edited-marker coverage remains
portable. Native Windows qualification is pending. This does not complete worker
dispatch or independent product acceptance.

### [ ] RELEASE-INVARIANTS-001 — Require SemVer release branches and verified public tags

- **Release blocker:** yes; applies equally to the framework and derived projects.
- **Observed failure:** The public repository advertises no tags, so default
  installed-CLI parent selection fails with `repository_lineage.release_unavailable`.
  Explicit-parent tutorial sessions did not exercise this first-run path.
- **Enforcement findings:** Release policy accepts `pep440`; branch ownership has
  an exemption when no default branch is configured. Published verification checks
  remote branch/tag revision equality but does not itself require the branch to
  be the version's release line. Remove exemptions, including legacy-policy paths.
  Canonical release identity must be SemVer; ecosystem-specific package spelling
  may only be a checked projection, not a competing release-version authority.
- **Publication distinction:** Development builds may exist without release tags,
  but neither an installer, migration, nor release receipt may represent such a
  build as a verified published release. Framework-managed release paths must fail
  closed; direct out-of-band Git/forge writes require forge protections and cannot
  be made impossible by a client CLI alone.
- **Dependency evidence:** Public PR #11 owns canonical-destination corrections
  and remains unmerged with CI pending at inspection. Do not duplicate its edits
  or treat its pre-merge checks as exact merged-source qualification. The public
  source snapshot still carries the old provider destination until that repair lands.
- **Next action:** Implement and test release invariants before publication;
  retain default-parent fail-closed behavior. Use source-matched tooling because
  the ambient 1.0.1 CLI cannot parse this checkout's `artifact_gate` policy.

- **Priority:** P0
- **Owner:** framework release core, inherited release policy, publication acceptance
- **Direction:** Every Literate AI project must use SemVer and release from a release branch with a tag on that branch; repair public bare init failure.

Remove branch-policy exemptions, require semantic release identity and remote branch/tag proof, and qualify fresh public installation without an explicit parent. Preserve private-history isolation and do not tag an unqualified snapshot.

worker-side intent registration can preserve direct library interface edges.
Identity-only context cannot implement that registration faithfully. This does
not by itself complete provider material transfer, private toolchain composition,
or production BUILD dispatch.

identity, Component revision, and generation key against the candidate before
launch. Missing plans, substituted plan bytes, internally consistent replacement
plans, and changed candidate generation keys are refused. All 38 focused BUILD
checks pass, including supervised child execution and CAS result transfer; the
12 artifact-admission checks also pass. This remains preparation for production
BUILD dispatch, not completion of that phase or the 1.2 program.

### Windows hardware challenge: receiver hash allocation overhead

Hosted run `36804231273` failed Windows shard 3 in two action-execution configuration
tests because hardware admission expired. Native Windows diagnosis on the
previously qualified `d25ef141` checkout measured imports at 4.141 seconds, one
receiver hash at 16.811 seconds, and actual hardware collection at 8.526 seconds.
The challenge hashes receiver code on both sides, consuming substantial margin
inside the existing 60-second bound. This identifies a contributor, not proof
that it is the only cause of the hosted failures.

The shared regular-file reader requested the remaining 64 MiB package budget for
each file. A 212-byte local file produced a 67,242,310-byte traced allocation peak.
A native Windows comparison over 655 files / 11,939,451 bytes took 16.513 seconds
with the current reader (15.880 seconds in file reads), versus 0.343 seconds with
reads bounded to descriptor size plus one byte; both produced the identical
receiver identity. Fix that allocation behavior and refuse changing file sizes.
Do not widen probe deadlines, skip real hardware admission, cache stale facts,
or replace file-content hashing with metadata-only identity checks.

Local validation of the implemented reader change passes three allocation/size
checks, all 36 source-cache tests, and all 167 action tests (125.658 seconds).
The same 212-byte file now peaks at 133,478 traced bytes rather than 67,242,310.
The reader preserves the exact maximum-size admission and content bytes, and
rejects growth or truncation after descriptor metadata capture. Exact-revision
Windows hardware/configuration qualification and hosted CI remain required before
claiming the hardware-admission failures resolved.

Native Windows qualification at `cd399ee0` passes 39 tests with one POSIX-only
FIFO skip: bounded regular files (3), action capabilities (11), hardware (9),
and action execution configuration (16 passed / 1 skipped). Both configuration
tests that failed the hosted run pass with their original deadlines. A separate
qualification on the same frozen revision passes all five BUILD child boundary
tests and all 44 BUILD tests, including the real supervised child and read-only
artifact cleanup. These are native regression results; current-head hosted CI,
complete worker readiness and the full 1.2 release qualification remain open.

### Portable artifact-tree ordering

Remaining BUILD transfer qualification exposed native `Path` sorting in the local
artifact-tree identity. Windows compares path components without case; POSIX uses
case-sensitive components. Identical portable trees containing `Z.txt` and `a.txt`
therefore receive different custody identities. Define ordering as case-sensitive
relative path components on every platform, preserving the existing POSIX identity
and file-content verification. Do not silently accept historical alternative tree
hashes: affected Windows artifacts must be rebuilt with current custody. Prove the
ordering on native Windows and keep cross-worker lifecycle qualification open.

Local evidence: the portable-order test checks mixed-case names, directory-prefix
ordering, reversed creation order and changed content against one exact custody
identity. It passes alongside all 12 transferred-build tests, all 44 BUILD tests,
12 version-authority tests, project validation and Ruff. Native Windows proof is
still required for this change.

### BUILD action envelope admission

Connect the existing supervised BUILD operation to lifecycle dispatch authority.
Before launching the private child, require the selected worker, current deadline,
canonical BUILD action/component/payload and its single PLAN predecessor to match
the exact admitted BUILD input. Reject missing, extra, oversized or substituted
records before process creation. Re-admit the returned BUILD result against that
same input before emitting it. Exercise this path with the real supervised child.
This is the receiver operation prerequisite; configured tool inventory, advertised
capability and shared-queue controller installation remain subsequent work.

Outcome: `execute_build_action` admits the exact dispatch envelope, invokes the
existing bounded supervisor and re-admits returned BUILD result bytes. All 48
BUILD tests pass, including a real child using the shared specialized port factory
through this receiver operation. Four new tests cover worker/phase/predecessor/
deadline mismatch, missing/extra/corrupt/oversized records, validly rehashed foreign
payloads, and an actual child echoing input instead of a result. Eleven architecture
and 12 version-authority tests, project validation and Ruff pass. The default action
CLI still does not advertise BUILD: private configuration, tool inventory admission,
source hydration and controller queue composition remain open.

### BUILD reservations in the production ready queue

The BUILD receiver operation is available, but the lifecycle currently submits all
BUILD calls directly to its executor. Add the same nonblocking reservation port
used by INDEX/AUTHORIZE/PLAN so an admitted BUILD adapter can share worker slots
without occupying threads while waiting for capacity. Preserve the current grant
guard immediately before reserved execution, release every reservation on success
or failure, and validate the returned Standard build output before TEST readiness.
Prove that exhausted BUILD capacity leaves other ready phases runnable. Installing
the configured command adapter remains required; this queue contract alone is not
remote BUILD support.

Outcome: the production BUILD stage recognizes `AdmittedComponentBuilder` and
reserves before entering the shared executor. Eleven readiness tests pass,
including exhausted BUILD capacity with other phases progressing and invalid
reserved output releasing its slot without reaching TEST. All 55 lifecycle,
19 shared-factory and 12 version-authority tests also pass; project validation,
Ruff and diff checks pass. The configured command builder and worker capability
admission remain uninstalled, so this is readiness plumbing, not a claim of
complete remote BUILD or 1.2 acceptance.

The controller stores finalized plans but retains full grants only for native SDK
builds. Remote BUILD requires the actual `StandardPlanFinalizationInputs`, not a
grant reconstructed from its identity. Retain the latest exact inputs alongside
each registered Component plan, whether finalized locally or accepted remotely.
Expose a data-only getter that rejects unregistered or superseded plans, changed
current contracts/providers/SDK custody and expired grants before yielding inputs.
Use this custody for subsequent command BUILD composition; do not relax execution
phase or tool binding checks.

Outcome: local and remotely accepted plans retain `StandardPlanFinalizationInputs`
by Component revision. `build_execution_inputs` checks the current plan, current
input projection and grant validity before returning the stored value. Four new
custody tests pass, including superseded plans, contract drift, grant expiry and
TEST-only data access without BUILD permission. All 48 BUILD tests, four native
SDK consumer-build tests (140.209 seconds), 19 factory tests and 12 version-authority
tests pass, along with project validation and Ruff. Command builder installation
and real remote handoff qualification remain open.

Implement the controller builder over the already admitted worker pool and shared

immediately before local artifact registration. Refuse missing evidence recording,

Outcome: `CommandComponentBuilder` uses the INDEX capacity owner, exact retained

rechecked after that potentially blocking admission check. Seven controller tests
pass through actual command transport, including a retained exact-input build

The fixture supplies BUILD admission and an already-built result explicitly; it

All 48 BUILD, 11 architecture and 12 version-authority checks also pass, with

### Configured BUILD receiver execution

Wire the BUILD action operation into the one-shot receiver through a typed trusted
startup configuration, never a request-selected import or command. Require current
privately observed launcher/tool bindings and exact compiler/BUILD tool selection
before fetching source or allocating job custody. Hydrate only the bounded verified
source manifest into CAS, then supervise a child in one owned job directory. Bind
CAS/workspace locations through supervisor-owned controls, refuse conflicting child
CLI locations, and remove still-owned job custody after normal completion or child
failure. Recheck current authorization and tool observations around the operation.
Default receivers remain unconfigured for BUILD; capability/inventory advertising
and automatic composition follow separately. Receiver parent death and recovery
remain explicit unfinished release obligations.

Outcome: the typed configured receiver now hydrates verified source blobs, selects
exact observed tools and supervises BUILD in an owned job directory. The real-child
fixture downloads source through HTTP after controller source removal and returns
verified build artifacts; its outer receiver is invoked in-process, so this is not
yet SSH qualification. Failure and cancellation remove read-only partial job files.
Supervisor path controls override inherited values, conflicting child CLI paths
refuse before input reads, and external or root-level artifact paths refuse before
BUILD while source/runtime contexts close. Four configured-worker, six child,
172 action, seven controller, 11 architecture and 12 version-authority tests pass,
along with project validation and Ruff. Default receivers explicitly report BUILD
as unconfigured. Next: bind configured capability discovery to the observed tool
inventory, then select compatible BUILD workers and install the controller adapter
with explicit result-CAS access. Full remote runtime composition and recovery remain
open.

Bind result transport explicitly per worker in private action configuration: either
